title: Defining the Grid: Columns & Rows 📏
description: Create explicit grid tracks with `grid-template-columns`, `grid-template-rows`, the `fr` unit, `repeat()`, and `minmax()`.

slides.title: `grid-template-columns` & `grid-template-rows` 📐
The `fr` Unit: Fractional Space 🧮
slides.content:
# Divide Available Space Proportionally

`fr` stands for fraction. It distributes the free space (after fixed tracks and gaps) according to the specified proportions.

```css
grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr 1fr;
/* Free space split: 1 + 2 + 1 = 4 parts.
   Column 1 gets 1/4, column 2 gets 2/4, column 3 gets 1/4. */
```
Unlike percentages, `fr` never overflows the container because it only uses leftover space. Combine with fixed widths for hybrid layouts.

quizData.question: With `grid-template-columns: 200px 1fr 2fr;` and a container width of 800px, how wide is the second column?

options.text: 200px (first) + remaining 600px split 1:2 → 200px and 400px, so second column 200px

quizData.explanation: Container 800px - 200px (col1) = 600px free. Split 1fr:2fr = 200px (col2) and 400px (col3). So col2 = 200px.

slides.title: `repeat()`: DRY Track Definitions 🔁
slides.content:
# Avoid Repetitive Values

Instead of writing `1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr`, use `repeat(4, 1fr)`.

```css
grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);   /* three equal columns */
grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 200px 1fr); /* two times the pattern 200px 1fr = four columns */
```
You can also use `auto-fill` and `auto-fit` for responsive, auto‑generated columns without media queries.

slides.title: `minmax()`: Flexible Tracks with Limits 🚧
slides.content:
# Set a Minimum and Maximum Size

`minmax(min, max)` defines a size range for a track. The track will never be smaller than `min` nor larger than `max`.

```css
grid-template-columns: minmax(200px, 1fr) 1fr;
/* First column: at least 200px, can grow to fill space. Second: 1fr of remaining. */
```
Combined with `auto-fill`/`auto-fit`, you get fully responsive grids without breakpoints.

quizData.question: `repeat(3, 1fr)` is equivalent to `1fr 1fr 1fr`.
quizData.explanation: `repeat()` simply repeats the track list the specified number of times.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use `fr` for Fluid Layouts

`fr` units are ideal for responsive designs. Combine with `minmax()` and `auto-fit` to create layouts that adapt without a single media query.
